en.title: Tariff proposals become concrete, but markets price the process—not the duty
en.deck: USTR's formal determinations and proposed tariffs move trade policy from speculation into consultation, while strong US quarterly growth, sticky PCE inflation, falling Treasury yields and a relief rally reveal a split market response. The latest FAO food index adds a divergent food-commodity signal: cereals eased while sugar rose sharply and food-assistance needs remained widespread.
en.regime: Global activity remains uneven; US quarterly demand is strong but monthly real consumption is flat, inflation remains elevated, and trade-policy uncertainty is interacting with technology and energy risk.
en.key_risk: Broad final tariff coverage or retaliation could increase landed costs and delay investment while sticky inflation limits monetary-policy flexibility; persistent energy disruption would add a separate price shock.

pt-BR.title: Tarifas propostas ganham forma, mas o mercado precifica o processo — não o imposto
pt-BR.deck: As determinações formais e as tarifas propostas pelo USTR levam a política comercial da especulação à consulta, enquanto crescimento trimestral americano forte, inflação PCE persistente, rendimentos menores dos Treasuries e recuperação das bolsas revelam uma resposta de mercado dividida. O último índice da FAO acrescenta um sinal divergente de commodities alimentares: cereais recuaram enquanto o açúcar subiu fortemente e a necessidade de assistência alimentar permaneceu ampla.

signal_rationale.delta: Compared with the 25 November edition, which covered tariff expectations before formal findings and the inflation-rate transmission, this edition updates the legal state to published determinations and proposed product-level actions, then tests the market response against the BEA's newly released Q3 GDP second estimate and October PCE. The 24 November issue's regional growth/steel dispersion and the 23 November China ore/steel inventory thesis are not repeated. The revision completes the food-commodity screen with FAO's 6 November October index: aggregate food prices fell 1.2% month on month while sugar rose 6.6% and 28.8% year on year; the latest cereal balance and 41-country external-assistance count add a distinct food-system qualification.
signal_rationale.evidence: USTR's 25 November notice lists determinations for 14 economies, proposed additional duties with exceptions/netting and a public-comment process through 5 January 2027. BEA released Q3 real GDP at 4.3% annualized and October PCE inflation at 3.8% headline/3.3% core. Reuters reports the 25 November equity/yield close and 26 November Asian rebound; Treasury/FRED reports the 10-year yield; Eurostat, IIF and worldsteel provide dated cross-region inflation, flows and output data. FAO's 6 November release reports FFPI 133.9 (-1.2% m/m, +5.9% y/y), cereal index 116.8 (-4.5% m/m), sugar 121.3 (+6.6% m/m, +28.8% y/y), 2026 cereal production forecast 2,999 Mt, 2026/27 trade -3.3% and 41 countries/territories requiring external food assistance.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Formal trade-policy findings affect product coverage and expected landed costs; firms adjust sourcing, inventories and investment; import prices and margins transmit to inflation and trade volumes; monetary expectations, yields, FX and cross-border funding respond.
signal_rationale.transmission: USTR determination → consultation/final coverage/effective date → tariff incidence and sourcing → import prices, margins, trade and capex → inflation expectations, central-bank reaction, yields, currencies and capital flows. Food commodities are heterogeneous: cereal quotations eased, sugar rose on Brazil weather-related harvest/crushing disruption and production concerns elsewhere; global export quotations pass through national currencies, transport, conflict and retail margins before affecting household affordability.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The thesis weakens if final coverage is narrow or delayed, net landed costs barely change, trade and capex remain stable, core goods inflation disinflates and energy shipping/export data show no sustained supply loss.

key_constraints: Tariffs remain proposed; product annexes, exclusions, effective dates and final negotiated changes must be monitored.
Market observations are from different reporting windows; US cash markets are closed on 26 November for Thanksgiving.
PCE, GDP, HICP and steel-output series have different scopes and cannot be treated as one comparable measure.
The IIF capital-flow estimate is October monthly data, not November daily flow.
Oil and shipping incident claims are attributed to Reuters and not independently verified in this report.

producer_checks.novelty_decision: The new delta is formal USTR determinations/proposed measures plus released BEA GDP/PCE data; this is not merely a calendar update to 25 November. The 24 November regional PMI/steel and 23 November China ore-inventory theses are not repeated.

reproducibility_notes.food: FAO 6 Nov 2026 October FFPI: 133.9 points, -1.2% m/m, +5.9% y/y, -16.4% from March 2022 peak. Cereal index 116.8 (-4.5% m/m, +12.6% y/y); vegetable oils 199.2 (+0.3% m/m); sugar 121.3 (+6.6% m/m, +28.8% y/y); meat -1.2% m/m; dairy -1.1% m/m. FAO forecast 2026 cereal production 2,999 Mt (second-highest), 2026/27 cereal trade 507.7 Mt (-3.3%) and stocks-to-use 32.4%; 41 countries/territories require external food assistance (31 in Africa). FFPI is an international traded-commodity index, not retail CPI or household affordability; production/trade numbers are forecasts.
